### Review

Review is Forgejo's pull request review: approve, or request changes and say what must change; a comment neither approves nor holds anything. A pull request into `main` of `paper-repo` waits for the owners of the paths it changes, and one into its `release` or `final` waits for the approval of `internal-review-repo`, the only one counted there, of the very commit it merges: a push to it after the approval withdraws it. A review request stands until its reviewer reviews, and a review until its reviewer reviews again: nobody withdraws or dismisses another's.

### Versions and release

A version for the world's users is a merge of `main` into `release` of `paper-repo`, by a pull request that `internal-review-repo` approved and whose checks pass. The system writes the checks as commit statuses on the pull request's head (`hutian/delivery`, and the world's contract's when it holds one), and a failing one says what is missing and who provides it; nobody else writes a status. Merge with a merge commit, not a squash or a rebase, or the next version conflicts. The system publishes each version as a release of `world/result`, the world's results, with the delivery attached: the users of the world read those releases and nothing else, and every role reads them. The last approval is a merge into `final` in the same way: the system releases the world from it, at once, and nothing pushed after it is part of it. Offer a `release` version as soon as the delivery holds its main work, so that `internal-review-repo`'s review comes while there is still room to act on it; `final` is the last. Do not ask another role to review the same unchanged delivery twice merely to pass through both branches. A release goes to the world's user; no role submits it to a venue or declares a licence for it.

When the world is quiet, the system hands each remaining gap of the delivery to its owner once, and once more when `main` of `paper-repo` has moved since; if it goes quiet again before a gap, a version, an open request or a review changes, the world ends there, unless a tracked job is still running, or the world runs to a wall-clock limit with someone outside attending it and all that is left is that `paper-repo` has proposed no version, with nothing failed and nothing open but requests that `ht-human` opened and their owners have seen: then it waits instead of ending, up to that limit. So whatever needs another role's action must be open where that role owns it.

\paragraph{Shapley attribution and its estimators.}
SHAP casts feature attribution as the Shapley value of a value function that removes features \citep{lundberg2017}; the value function may be marginal or conditional \citep{chen2020,sundararajan2020,kumar2020}, and removal-based explanations share this structure \citep{covert2020removal}.
Model-agnostic estimation is randomised: Kernel SHAP and its unbiased variant with variance and convergence estimates \citep{covert2021}, permutation and antithetic sampling \citep{mitchell2022}, Leverage SHAP with guarantees \citep{musco2025}, regression-adjusted Monte Carlo \citep{witter2025regadj} and SHAP-IQ \citep{fumagalli2023}; \citet{chen2023algorithms} survey the algorithms.
Tree ensembles admit a deterministic algorithm \citep{lundberg2020trees}.
These works report the error to the exact Shapley value, usually in $\ell_2$ and averaged over instances, at chosen budgets.
They do not ask whether one run at a deployment budget supports the conclusion a reader draws from it for a given instance, nor whether the run can detect its own failure.

\paragraph{Top-$k$ identification.}
Whether an estimated ordering yields the right top-$k$ is asked from the estimator side: Shapley bandits for top-$k$ identification \citep{kolpaczki2021bandits} and antithetic sampling for top-$k$ Shapley identification \citep{kolpaczki2025antithetic} design algorithms with sampling guarantees.
We instead measure deployed default estimators on trained tabular models and map the conditions under which one run identifies the right features.
\citet{covert2021} already give within-run variance and convergence detection, so what we add to the single-run check is its validation against the top-$k$ conclusion.
\citet{huang2023} question what Shapley values say about a model; we only bound scope by holding the value function fixed.

\paragraph{Disagreement and robustness.}
\citet{krishna2022} and \citet{neely2021} study disagreement between explanation methods; \citet{alvarez2018} and \citet{ghorbani2019fragile} study sensitivity to input perturbation; \citet{visani2022lime} study LIME stability under resampling; \citet{yuan2022} study background size for deep models.
We fix the model, the value function and the instance, and isolate the explainer's own randomness against an exact reference, then compare it with background and retraining noise.

\paragraph{Multiplicity as a yardstick.}
Predictive multiplicity and the Rashomon set \citep{marx2020,fisher2019,dong2020cloud} give the variability between equally accurate models; ShapleyVIC \citep{shapleyvic2022} applies this to Shapley importance.
We use it as a noise floor for explainer noise, not as the target.
For a tabular model, a SHAP value per feature is estimated once by a randomised, budget-limited algorithm, and the reader draws a conclusion from that single result: which feature mattered most, which three mattered, whether a feature pushed the score up or down.
The literature on Shapley estimators measures how close an estimate is to the exact Shapley value, usually in $\ell_2$, averaged over instances and at chosen budgets \citep{lundberg2017,covert2021,mitchell2022,musco2025}.
A small average error does not say that a particular run returns the conclusion the exact values would give: when two features are nearly tied, a tiny error swaps them.
